chapter_theme: Songs at Oothimalai (ஊதிமலை): the poet, ignorant of the Siva Agamas and given to the desire for women, asks for mercy, firm knowledge and instruction; the praise makes Murugan the teacher who spoke the Vedic mantra into Siva's ear and the light that is the life of the letter Om.

611.reading: The poet asks to be able to worship Murugan, the son given by the primal Mahamayi Ambai who delighted Siva, as the Lord of grace; he confesses that he has wandered through the five elements without knowing the full Siva Agamas, thinking only of the desires of women and wanting pleasure, and asks Murugan to pity him so that the path of right may shine. The praise names Murugan as the one who spoke the Vedic mantra into Siva's ear and came on the blue peacock, and who, to end the karma of those who practise the yoga taught by Veda and Agama, grew as their flesh and life and gave them life with sound, at Oothimalai.
611.nuance: The fault named is ignorance of the Agamas (பூரண சிவாகமங்கள் அறியாதே) as much as lust. சிவனார் திகழ்ந்த காதில் உரை வேத மந்த்ர is the Siva-teaching story as a whisper in the ear. ஊனும் உயிராய் வளர்ந்து ஓசையுடன் வாழ்வு தந்த may play on the shrine's name (ஊதி, 'blowing'): the Lord as the body, life and sound of the yogi; the sense is uncertain.

612.reading: The poet asks not to think in his heart of the petty pleasure of women with combed, heavy hair buns, deceitful and charming, but for Murugan to destroy his weak mind, give firm knowledge and stand gracious where he tells Murugan's deeds. The praise names Murugan nephew of Vishnu, the father of four-faced Brahma; the guru son of the Lord; the dancer to drum syllables who gives mercy to the soul that leaves the inert body; and the bright light who is the restraint of the recited letters, the mercy to devotees and the breath of the letter Om, at Oothi hill.
612.nuance: கோழை மனத்தைக் கெடுத்து வன்புல ஞான குணத்தைக் கொடுத்து: a weak mind exchanged for a firm knowledge. ஓம் எனும் எழுத்துக்கு உயிர்ப்பும் என் சுடர் ஒளியோனே makes Murugan the breath of Om, and நாத நிலைக்குள் the state of nada. The lines on the trouble at the sacrifice (நாடு மகத்து எற்கு இடுக்கண்) and on the soul leaving the body (சடத்தில் நின்று உயிரான துறத்தற்கு) are hard to construe.
